'''William Robert Breckon Lionheart''' is a British applied mathematician specialising in inverse problems, tomographic imaging, and low‑frequency electromagnetic sensing. He is Professor of Applied Mathematics at the University of Manchester.<ref name ="ORCID">{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= 17 July 2026|title= William Lionheart|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0971-4678 |website=ORCID |access-date=19 July 2026}}</ref> His research spans theoretical, numerical, and practical aspects of inverse problems with applications in medicine, industry, security, and non‑destructive testing.

==Early life and education==
Lionheart attended [[Larkmead School]] in [[Abingdon-on-Thames]] as a child, then  studied mathematics at the [[University of Warwick]], receiving a 1st class hons B.Sc. degree.<ref name="ORCID"/> He completed his Ph.D. at Oxford Brookes University in 1990 under the supervision of Michael Pidcock working on problems in [[Electrical Impedance Tomography]].<ref>{{cite web |title=William Robert Breckon Lionheart |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=96456 |website=Math Genealogy Project |access-date=2026-07-05}}</ref>

==Academic career==
Lionheart began his academic career at [[Oxford Polytechnic]] (later Oxford Brookes University), where he worked as a lecturer and senior lecturer.  In 1999 he joined UMIST as Lecturer in Applied Mathematics, becoming Reader in 2002. Following the merger that created the modern University of Manchester, he was appointed Professor of Applied Mathematics in 2005.<ref name="ORCID" />

Lionheart worked extensively on Electrical Impedance Tomography, especially in a biomedical setting. His contributions include theoretical results on uniqueness of solution for boundary shape <ref name="Lionheart1998">{{cite journal | last=Lionheart | first=W R B | title=Boundary shape and electrical impedance tomography | journal=Inverse Problems | volume=14 | issue=1 | date=1998-02-01 | issn=0266-5611 | doi=10.1088/0266-5611/14/1/012 | pages=139–147 | bibcode=1998InvPr..14..139L | url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0266-5611/14/1/012 | access-date=2026-07-19| url-access=subscription }}</ref> and  anisotropic conductivity,<ref name="Lionheart2004">{{cite book | last=Lionheart | first=W. R. B. | title=New Analytic and Geometric Methods in Inverse Problems | chapter=Geometric Methods for Anisotropic Inverse Boundary Value Problems | publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg | publication-place=Berlin, Heidelberg | date=2004 | isbn=978-3-642-07379-3 | doi=10.1007/978-3-662-08966-8_12 | chapter-url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-662-08966-8_12 | access-date=2026-07-19 | pages=337–351}}</ref><ref name="Gaburro2009">{{cite journal | last1=Gaburro | first1=Romina | last2=Lionheart | first2=William R B | title=Recovering Riemannian metrics in monotone families from boundary data | journal=Inverse Problems | volume=25 | issue=4 | date=2009-04-01 | issn=0266-5611 | doi=10.1088/0266-5611/25/4/045004 | article-number=045004 | bibcode=2009InvPr..25d5004G | url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0266-5611/25/4/045004 | access-date=2026-07-19| url-access=subscription }}</ref> numerical algorithms for reconstruction,<ref name="lionheart2004">{{cite journal | last=Lionheart | first=William R B | title=EIT reconstruction algorithms: pitfalls, challenges and recent developments | journal=Physiological Measurement | volume=25 | issue=1 | date=2004-02-01 | issn=0967-3334 | doi=10.1088/0967-3334/25/1/021 | pages=125–142 | pmid=15005311 | arxiv=physics/0310151 | url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0967-3334/25/1/021 | access-date=2026-07-19}}</ref> and reconstruction software <ref name="p486">{{cite journal | last1=Adler | first1=Andy | last2=Lionheart | first2=William R B | title=Uses and abuses of EIDORS: an extensible software base for EIT | journal=Physiological Measurement | volume=27 | issue=5 | date=2006-05-01 | issn=0967-3334 | doi=10.1088/0967-3334/27/5/S03 | pages=S25–S42 | pmid=16636416 | bibcode=2006PhyM...27S..25A | url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0967-3334/27/5/S03 | access-date=2026-07-19}}</ref> including being a founder member of the [[EIDORS]] project.

Lionheart worked on [[CT scan|X-ray tomography]] reconstruction especially for airport baggage screening, developing algorithms for a widely used fast tomography system with [[Rapiscan Systems]].<ref name="Thompson2015">{{cite journal | last1=Thompson | first1=William M | last2=Lionheart | first2=William R B | last3=Morton | first3=Edward J | last4=Cunningham | first4=Mike | last5=Luggar | first5=Russell D | title=High speed imaging of dynamic processes with a switched source x-ray CT system | journal=Measurement Science and Technology | volume=26 | issue=5 | date=2015-05-01 | issn=0957-0233 | doi=10.1088/0957-0233/26/5/055401 | article-number=055401 | bibcode=2015MeScT..26e5401T | url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0957-0233/26/5/055401 | access-date=2026-07-19}}</ref>  He sits on the Executive Board of the Collaborative Computational Imaging (CCPi) project <ref name="CCPi">{{cite web |url=https://www.ccpi.ac.uk/people/ |title=People |work=Executive Board |publisher=CCPi |access-date=2026-07-19 }}</ref> that develops the Core  Imaging Library (CIL) A  python framework for tomographic imaging [https://github.com/TomographicImaging/CIL].

In 2023 Lionheart led a programme at the [[Isaac Newton Institute]] in Cambridge entitled "Rich and Nonlinear Tomography - a multidisciplinary approach" [https://www.newton.ac.uk/event/rnt/].  He led held an EPSRC project [https://gtr.ukri.org/projects?ref=EP%2FV007742%2F1] 'Rich Nonlinear Tomography for advanced materials' a joint project between Manchester, Oxford and Cambridge. In this context ''Rich Tomography''  means rather than creating a simple scalar field one images a vector or tensor field, or a spectrum, or orientation density function.   Examples include  polarimetric tomography of magnetic fields,<ref name="Desai">{{cite journal | last1=Desai | first1=Naeem M | last2=Lionheart | first2=William R B | last3=Sales | first3=Morten | last4=Strobl | first4=Markus | last5=Schmidt | first5=Søren | title=Polarimetric neutron tomography of magnetic fields: uniqueness of solution and reconstruction | journal=Inverse Problems | volume=36 | issue=4 | date=2020-04-01 | issn=0266-5611 | doi=10.1088/1361-6420/ab44e0 | page=045001 | arxiv=1903.10884 | bibcode=2020InvPr..36d5001D | url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1361-6420/ab44e0 | access-date=2026-07-19}}</ref> X-ray diffraction tomography for strain imaging,<ref name=Lionheart2015>{{cite journal | last1=Lionheart | first1=W R B | last2=Withers | first2=P J | title=Diffraction tomography of strain | journal=Inverse Problems | volume=31 | issue=4 | date=2015-04-01 | issn=0266-5611 | doi=10.1088/0266-5611/31/4/045005 | article-number=045005 | bibcode=2015InvPr..31d5005L | url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0266-5611/31/4/045005 | access-date=2026-07-19}}</ref> and strain tomography with polarized light <ref name="Lionheart2009">Lionheart, William, and V. Sharafutdinov. "Reconstruction algorithm for the polarization tomography problem with incomplete data." Imaging Microstructures: Mathematical and Computational Challenges. American Mathematical Society, 2009. 137-160.</ref>

[[Magnetic induction tomography]] is closely related to EIT but a system of coils is used apply low frequency magnetic fields to image the conductivity 
of a body.  As well as his interest in MIT for medical imaging<ref name="Soleimani2006">{{cite journal | last1=Soleimani | first1=Manuchehr | last2=Lionheart | first2=William R. B | title=Absolute Conductivity Reconstruction in Magnetic Induction Tomography Using a Nonlinear Method | journal=IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging | volume=25 | issue=12 | date=2006 | issn=0278-0062 | doi=10.1109/TMI.2006.884196 | pages=1521–1530 | pmid=17167989 | bibcode=2006ITMI...25.1521S }}</ref> Lionheart has worked on applications in industrial process monitoring, such as flow of molten steel.<ref name="Soleimani2007">{{cite journal | last1=Soleimani | first1=Manuchehr | last2=Lionheart | first2=William R. B. | last3=Peyton | first3=Anthony J. | title=Image Reconstruction for High-Contrast Conductivity Imaging in Mutual Induction Tomography for Industrial Applications | journal=IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement | volume=56 | issue=5 | date=2007 | issn=0018-9456 | doi=10.1109/TIM.2007.895598 | pages=2024–2032 | bibcode=2007ITIM...56.2024S }}</ref>  Lionheart and collaborators have also worked on the theory the location and recognition of [[landmines]] using low frequency inductive methods <ref name="u033">{{cite journal | last1=Ledger | first1=Paul David | last2=Lionheart | first2=William R.B. | title=Generalised magnetic polarizability tensors | journal=Mathematical Methods in the Applied Sciences | volume=41 | issue=8 | date=2018-05-30 | issn=0170-4214 | doi=10.1002/mma.4809 | pages=3175–3196 | arxiv=1705.00580 | bibcode=2018MMAS...41.3175L | url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mma.4809 | access-date=2026-07-19}}</ref> as well as [[unexploded ordnance]].<ref name="Ledger2022">{{cite journal | last1=Ledger | first1=P. D. | last2=Lionheart | first2=W. R. B. | title=Minimal Object Characterizations Using Harmonic Generalized Polarizability Tensors and Symmetry Groups | journal=SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics | volume=82 | issue=6 | date=2022-12-31 | issn=0036-1399 | doi=10.1137/22M1471547 | pages=2057–2079 | url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/22M1471547 | access-date=2026-07-19}}</ref> With Prof Tony Peyton, Lionheart founded a laboratory for developing land mine detection technology funded by Sir [[Bobby Charlton]]'s charity "Find a Better Way" <ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.socialresponsibility.manchester.ac.uk/all-news/legacy-news/sir-bobby-charltons-dream-of-a-landmine-free-world-takes-leap-forward/ | title= Sir Bobby Charlton backs opening of international landmine research centre in Manchester|access-date=2026-08-03}}</ref>

==Awards, fellowships and prizes==
Lionheart was awarded a [[Harkness Fellowship]] in 1983 which enabled him to study at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name="ORCID"/>
In 2009 he accepted the Martin Black Prize<ref name="MBP">{{cite web |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/journal/0967-3334/page/Martin_Black_award |title=Martin Black award |work=Physiological Measurement |publisher=Institute of Physics |access-date=2026-07-19 }}</ref> on behalf of the team that devised `GREIT', a unified approach to 2D linear EIT reconstruction of lung images.<ref name="Adler2009">{{cite journal | last1=Adler | first1=Andy | last2=Arnold | first2=John H | last3=Bayford | first3=Richard | last4=Borsic | first4=Andrea | last5=Brown | first5=Brian | last6=Dixon | first6=Paul | last7=Faes | first7=Theo J C | last8=Frerichs | first8=Inéz | last9=Gagnon | first9=Hervé | last10=Gärber | first10=Yvo | last11=Grychtol | first11=Bartłomiej | last12=Hahn | first12=Günter | last13=Lionheart | first13=William R B | last14=Malik | first14=Anjum | last15=Patterson | first15=Robert P | last16=Stocks | first16=Janet | last17=Tizzard | first17=Andrew | last18=Weiler | first18=Norbert | last19=Wolf | first19=Gerhard K | title=GREIT: a unified approach to 2D linear EIT reconstruction of lung images | journal=Physiological Measurement | volume=30 | issue=6 | date=2009-06-01 | issn=0967-3334 | doi=10.1088/0967-3334/30/6/S03 | pages=S35–S55 | pmid=19491438 | bibcode=2009PhyM...30S..35A | url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0967-3334/30/6/S03 | access-date=2026-07-19}}</ref><ref name="Manchester2010">{{cite press release |url=https://www.manchester.ac.uk/about/news/manchester-mathematician-picks-up-medical-paper-prize/ |title=Manchester mathematician picks up medical paper prize |author=Daniel Cochlin |location=Manchester. UK |publisher=[[University of Manchester]] |date=2010-09-29 }}</ref>   Lionheart's team  won the defence and security category at the Engineer’s Technology and Innovation Awards for their work on the Rapiscan RTT baggage scanner.<ref name="MEN2013">{{cite news |last=McKeegan |first=Alice |url=http://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/local-news/a-clear-winner-the-high-speed-new-scanner-850776 |title=A clear winner: The high-speed new scanner for airports |work=[[Manchester Evening News]] |publisher=Manchester Evening News |date=2013-01-11 }}</ref> During 2013 and 2014 Lionheart visited [[Per Christain Hansen]] at the [[Technical University of Denmark]], with an [[Otto Mønsted]] visiting Fellowship.<ref name="DTU">{{cite press release |url=https://www.dtu.dk/english/news/all-news/nyhed?id=e067bc77-427b-4053-bc4d-649046c6e59enchester.ac.uk/about/news/manchester-mathematician-picks-up-medical-paper-prize/ |title=11 new international visiting professors |last=Tonsberg |first= Claus |location=Manchester. UK |publisher=DTU |date=2013-09-19 }}</ref> In 2015 Lionheart was awarded a [[Royal Society Wolfson Fellowship|Royal Society Wolfson Research merit Award]] for Novel Methods in Tomography imaging: "Rich tomography" and fast dynamic imaging.<ref name="WRM">{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2015/03/wolfson-research-merit-awards-march/ |title=Royal Society announces recipients of prestigious Wolfson Research Merit Awards |work=News from the Royal Society |publisher=[[The Royal Society]] |date=2015-03-12 |access-date=2026-07-19 }}</ref>

==Name==
Early publications appear under the name '''W. R. Breckon'''.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Breckon, W. R. |title=On uniqueness in electrical impedance tomography |journal=IMA Journal of Applied Mathematics |year=1988 |mr=0933790}}</ref>
By the early 1990s his papers appear under the name '''W. R. B. Lionheart'''.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Lionheart, W. R. B. |title=Uniqueness results in EIT |journal=Inverse Problems |year=1991 |mr=1435872}}</ref>
ORCID also lists both names as author aliases.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0971-4678 |title=ORCID profile: William R. B. Lionheart |access-date=2026-07-05}}</ref>
